A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title. All 40 pages, including Appendices A-G, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, perplexity, throughput and memory measurements in Section 8, plus gradient-rank analysis, ablations and pretrained-checkpoint analysis in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1-4, the training and throughput plots, and the appendix ablations and checkpoint analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4-6 retain the same shared-subspace compression, embedding decomposition, Grassmann updates and modified AdamW optimizer. The title change does not introduce or revise a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText, BookCorpus, OpenWebText and C4, with the same low-bandwidth and geographically distributed training scenarios. Appendix G retains the same pretrained-checkpoint coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same centralized and uncompressed decentralized comparators. Figure 6 retains no compression, Top-K, SVD and quantization, with no comparator added or removed.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, model configurations, bandwidth simulations and training settings are unchanged. This includes Table 1's 12-hour comparisons and Table 2's 640M-parameter, 12-billion-token evaluation.

E4.justification: The depth, batch-size, context-length and memory-scaling analyses are retained. Appendix F keeps the same Grassmann-update and fixed-embedding ablations, while Appendices C.1 and G retain the same rank analyses.

E5.justification: The experimental reporting practice is unchanged: the same point estimates and curves appear, without added seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and Figures 1-16 retain their numerical results and findings. For example, Table 2 reports compressed-model C4/BookCorpus perplexities of 12.53/12.67 versus 12.61/12.79 for the centralized baseline in both versions.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Statements 7.1-7.4 and proofs in Appendices A-E are unchanged, including the stochastic extension in Theorem E.2. Minor spacing differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about up to 100-fold communication efficiency, preserved convergence and geographically distributed 8B-model training. Retitling the paper does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning rank collapse, implicit regularization, computation versus communication costs and memory overhead are unchanged. No substantive applicability boundary, failure condition or limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information remains unchanged, including GPipe/TorchTitan usage, GPU configurations, hyperparameters and the 500-iteration subspace-update interval. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and related-work discussions throughout the appendices retain the same cited works and research positioning. The title rename does not revise the relationship to prior methods.

P1.justification: The title and running headers replace 'Protocol Models' with 'Subspace Networks'; copyright and arXiv version/date markings are updated. Body prose and section organization remain unchanged, and the keywords still include 'Protocol Models'.

P2.justification: There are small typographic spacing changes, most visibly tighter lettering in Figure 16's model labels. The same figures and tables retain their plots, panel arrangements, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 principally retitles the paper and updates date markings and minor typography. The methods, empirical evidence, proofs, interpretations and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. These cosmetic edits make no meaningful net difference to overall paper quality.
